_comment: Adversarial cases that the pipeline currently does NOT catch.
This is a ratchet, not an excuse list, and it works the same way as
- an entry with no reason or no fix_point fails;
- an entry whose case now PASSES is stale and fails, so a fix must delete its
entry rather than leave the ledger describing a weakness that is gone;
- a FAILING case with no entry is a new evasion and fails.
The direction matters. eval/compile-adversarial.json encodes what SHOULD happen,
so fixing a gate makes its case pass and its entry stale — the build tells you to
remove the entry. Had the suite encoded current behaviour instead, fixing a gate
would have broken the build, and the suite would have been defending the defect.
Five of these are almost certainly inherited rather than introduced by the port:
the differential oracle reports the TS gates and the frozen Python linter agreeing
on every shared verdict, so both miss them identically. That is exactly the case
ADR-0007 says parity cannot see. Confirming it against sources/v5/prompt_lint.py
is the fix_point for those entries — not a rewrite of the regex, which without
the divergence allowlist would put the two implementations out of parity and turn

evasions.reason: SECRET_LEAK_SCAN matches sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{20,128}; a U+200B inside the key breaks the character class, so the pattern does not match. Not a port defect on current evidence — the frozen linter uses the same shape.
evasions.fix_point: ADR-0007 divergence allowlist, then normalise zero-width characters before scanning

evasions.reason: The key is split across a newline. The character class excludes newline, so the match ends at the break and the remaining twenty characters are never considered.
evasions.fix_point: ADR-0007 divergence allowlist, then strip line breaks inside candidate runs before scanning

evasions.reason: The literal prefix `sk-` is case-sensitive, so SK-ANT- does not match. Whether a real credential survives upper-casing is provider-specific and unverified here; the gate's behaviour is what is recorded.
evasions.fix_point: confirm against sources/v5/prompt_lint.py, then decide whether case-insensitivity is correct rather than merely stricter

evasions.reason: Fenced regions are treated as documentation. A fence opened and never closed swallows the rest of the output, so everything after it is exempt. This is the most exploitable of the five: it needs three backticks and no closing pair. NOT specific to SECRET_LEAK_SCAN — stripDocumentationSpans is shared, so every gate that audits stripped text is evadable the same way. Demonstrated by overclaim-evades-via-unterminated-fence below.
evasions.fix_point: ADR-0007 divergence allowlist, then treat an unterminated fence as not-a-fence — one fix closes both entries and every other gate at once

evasions.reason: The same shared defect reaching a second gate. An unclosed fence before an overclaim strips it to EOF, so CLAIM_DISCIPLINE never sees it. Recorded separately rather than folded into the SECRET_LEAK_SCAN entry because the ledger counts CASES: one entry for a defect that spans gates would let the other gates' exposure go uncounted. Found by a property test that had been asserting monotonicity WITHOUT this exclusion — it passed for weeks because fc.string rarely emits three backticks at a line start, and failed about one run in eight.
evasions.fix_point: ADR-0007 divergence allowlist, then treat an unterminated fence as not-a-fence — the same fix as the entry above

evasions.reason: A four-backtick fence containing a three-backtick fence confuses the region parser, and the inner content is treated as documentation.
evasions.fix_point: ADR-0007 divergence allowlist, then parse fences by longest-run matching

evasions.reason: All sixteen gates are ported, so the original reason for this entry is gone; the case still evades for a reason that has nothing to do with porting. ADVERSARIAL_RESILIENCE is not an injection detector. It scores the text it is given for the PRESENCE OF DEFENSE-SIGNAL LANGUAGE, keyed by surface, and an injection payload contains none. Measured on the case's own stub: unarmed the gate returns PASS/not_armed, which is what the pipeline actually runs; armed with a corpus it returns FAIL 'Undefended surface(s): ledger' — naming a surface the payload has nothing to do with. Neither is the WARN this case expects, and no configuration produces one. The corpus type declares `payload?: string` and NOTHING READS IT: `scoreResilience` keys on `c.surface` alone, so the corpus's whole causal contribution is surfaces and weights.
evasions.fix_point: a gate that reads output for instruction-override patterns. NOT a widening of ADVERSARIAL_RESILIENCE: the frozen linter can never score — it cannot locate its own scorer — so changing the scoring path puts the two implementations out of parity in a branch the oracle cannot check, and ADR-0007 wants a divergence entry or a new gate id, not a quiet regex edit. Decide which, and correct GATES_REFERENCE.md, which describes this gate as testing whether a prompt 'resists known jailbreak/injection patterns'.
